title: Countable directed enlargement closed under a chosen function
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty partially ordered set such that every pair of elements has an upper bound in $I$. Let $s:I\to I$ be a function, with no monotonicity assumption, and let $S\subseteq I$ be an at most countable subset. There exists an at most countable nonempty subset $J\subseteq I$ such that $S\subseteq J$, $s(J)\subseteq J$, and for every $i,j\in J$ there is $k\in J$ with $i\le k$ and $j\le k$. Thus $J$ is directed with its inherited order; $S$ may be empty and $I$ need not itself be countable. Here at most countable means that the underlying type admits an injection into $\mathbf N$ [def-sfb-countable-set].

source.place: Tag 059W (lemma-ML-countable-colimit), proof, successive countable stabilization and directed-enlargement sets and their union; abstracted from the index-set construction.

proof.text: Choose $i_*\in I$. By the upper-bound hypothesis and classical choice, choose $b:I\times I\to I$ with $i\le b(i,j)$ and $j\le b(i,j)$ for every $i,j\in I$. Define subsets by recursion on $n\in\mathbf N$: $T_0=S\cup\{i_*\}$ and $T_{n+1}=T_n\cup s(T_n)\cup\{b(i,j):i,j\in T_n\}$. All terms are subsets of $I$, since $s$ and $b$ take values in $I$. The defining union gives $T_n\subseteq T_{n+1}$, and induction on $m-n$ gives $T_n\subseteq T_m$ whenever $n\le m$.

source.place: Tag 059W (lemma-ML-countable-colimit), proof, successive countable enlargements and their union; explicit set-theoretic expansion of the index-set argument.

proof.text: Every singleton is at most countable by [def-sfb-countable-set]: its unique map to $\{0\}\subseteq\mathbf N$ is injective. Thus $T_0$ is at most countable by the binary-union clause of [lem-trf-countable-unions]. Suppose $T_n$ is at most countable. Write $s(T_n)=\bigcup_{i\in T_n}\{s(i)\}$ and $\{b(i,j):i,j\in T_n\}=\bigcup_{i\in T_n}\bigcup_{j\in T_n}\{b(i,j)\}$. The restricted-union clause of the same lemma makes the first set countable, and two applications make the second set countable (first for each fixed $i$, then over $i$). Two binary unions now make $T_{n+1}$ at most countable. Induction proves countability of every $T_n$. Set $J=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbf N}T_n$; the sequence-union clause makes $J$ at most countable. No countability of the ambient $I$ was used.

source.place: Tag 059W (lemma-ML-countable-colimit), proof, successive countable enlargements and their union; explicit set-theoretic expansion of the index-set argument.

proof.text: As $S\subseteq T_0\subseteq J$ and $i_*\in T_0\subseteq J$, the set $J$ contains $S$ and is nonempty, even when $S=\varnothing$. If $i\in J$, choose $n$ with $i\in T_n$. Then $s(i)\in s(T_n)\subseteq T_{n+1}\subseteq J$. Hence $s(J)\subseteq J$; no comparison between $s(i)$ and $s(j)$ was used.

source.place: Tag 059W (lemma-ML-countable-colimit), proof, successive countable enlargements and their union; explicit set-theoretic expansion of the index-set argument.

proof.text: For $i,j\in J$, choose $n,m\in\mathbf N$ with $i\in T_n$ and $j\in T_m$. Put $r=\max(n,m)$. The inclusions from Step 1 put both $i$ and $j$ in $T_r$. Consequently $k=b(i,j)$ lies in $T_{r+1}\subseteq J$, while the choice of $b$ gives $i\le k$ and $j\le k$. This proves directedness in the inherited order, with an upper bound lying in $J$ itself.
